content: Neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B sulfate, and gramicidin are components of an antiseptic solution approved by the FDA for treating superficial infections of the external eye and its adnexa caused by susceptible bacteria. Common adverse reactions include itching, swelling, and conjunctival erythema. For adults, the FDA-approved indication for NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution is the topical treatment of superficial infections such as conjunctivitis, keratitis, keratoconjunctivitis, blepharitis, and blepharoconjunctivitis. The recommended dosage is one or two drops in the affected eye every 4 hours for 7 to 10 days. In severe infections, the dosage may be increased to two drops every hour. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B sulfate, and gramicidin in both adult and pediatric patients. Similarly, there is limited data on FDA-labeled indications and dosages for pediatric patients. NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to any of its components. It is not intended for injection into the eye, including the anterior chamber or subconjunctival space. Topical antibiotics, particularly neomycin sulfate, may cause cutaneous sensitization, with symptoms such as itching, redness, and conjunctival or eyelid edema. Sensitization may also present as a failure to heal. Long-term use requires periodic examination for these signs, and the medication should be discontinued if observed. Symptoms typically resolve quickly upon withdrawal of the medication. Adverse reactions reported post-marketing include allergic sensitization reactions such as itching, swelling, and conjunctival erythema. Rarely, more serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. Local irritation upon instillation has also been noted. There is no established information on drug interactions, use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution is classified as Pregnancy Category C, meaning animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, and its effects on fetal harm or reproductive capacity are unknown. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. There is no guidance on its use in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised populations. The solution is administered topically, and there is limited information on monitoring, IV compatibility, or overdose. In case of suspected overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline immediately. Pharmacologically, the solution provides a broad spectrum of antibacterial action through the combined effects of its components. Neomycin inhibits protein synthesis by binding to ribosomal RNA, causing misreading of bacterial genetic code. Polymyxin B disrupts the bacterial cell membrane by interacting with its phospholipid components. Gramicidin increases bacterial cell membrane permeability to inorganic cations by forming channels in the lipid bilayer. Together, these agents are active against organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus, streptococci (including Streptococcus pneumoniae), Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Klebsiella/Enterobacter species, Neisseria species, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. However, the product does not provide adequate coverage against Serratia marcescens. NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution is supplied as a sterile antimicrobial solution for ophthalmic use in a 10 mL plastic dispenser bottle. It should be stored at 15° to 25°C (59° to 77°F) and protected from light. There is no established interaction between alcohol and this medication. Patients should consult their doctor regarding alcohol use while on this medication. The brand name for this product is NEOSPORIN®.
